description: tsib is a Forschungszentrum Jülich Python package for generating consistent residential-building demand and production series. It combines occupancy behaviour, appliance electricity demand, a 5R1C thermal model, solar production and location-specific weather. Users configure individual buildings or select archetypes; outputs include occupancy, electricity, heat, photovoltaic and solar-thermal time series. Coverage is configurable but the documented application and default inputs centre on German residential buildings, including TABULA archetypes and DWD reference years. Public source and pip installation are free under MIT. A limitation is that thermal calculations require a MILP solver, with CBC the documented default. Flexible Copernicus weather access also requires registration and agreement to the upstream data terms. Generated profiles are modelled assumptions, not customer measurements. tsib can initialise demand and distributed-generation scenarios for building and grid simulations, complementary to EnergyPlus (model-energyplus). Its README identifies the component models and provides an example notebook. No weather files, archetype data or occupancy series were downloaded.
